source.title: Applying Cyclical Learning Rate to Neural Machine Translation
source.authors: Choon Meng Lee; Jianfeng Liu; Wei Peng

record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer and batch-size effects on transformer-based neural machine translation, extending related image-classification results to translation tasks.
record.gate_note: Reports BLEU comparisons across learning-rate policies and describes batch-size outcomes under cyclical learning rates. Cited results about other methods are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and SGD held-out BLEU under learning-rate tuning and examines batch-size effects under CLR in transformer translation models, a new setting for V4 and V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they conclude that CLR improves transformer NMT test performance and permits larger batches without harming generalization, while emphasizing optimizer and schedule selection. The batch-size evidence shown here is validation loss rather than batch-specific test BLEU.
record.recipe_differences: Uses triangular cyclical learning rates with Adam or SGD for transformer NMT on IWSLT translation corpora; compares with inverse square-root schedules. The paper reports best BLEU and batch-size behavior rather than random-label fitting or generalization-gap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Corpus and optimizer learning-rate policy affect BLEU; Adam is sensitive to excessive learning rates; SGD requires the no-shrink option in the reported CLR experiments. Under CLR, batch size 256 diverges while larger batch sizes perform better.

fits_no_version.finding: Shrinking CLR lowers BLEU relative to unshrunk CLR within Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLR decay choices affect transformer translation performance; a within-optimizer schedule comparison alone does not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD disadvantage.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA loss-landscape visualizations qualitatively illustrate optimization trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLR may help optimization traverse plateaus; these visualizations do not test magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.

record.problems: The study uses three IWSLT translation settings and reports no uncertainty estimates. The batch-size outcome is described in text but the supplied text gives no numerical values for Figure 6.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Image classification, word-level language modeling, matched training performance, broader hyperparameter tuning beyond learning-rate policies, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
The large-batch penalty without CLR; longer training, normalization changes, and other adaptations. Batch-size-specific test BLEU is not reported in the supplied text.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.

missing.what: Separate outcomes for larger batch sizes in Figure 6, including their exact batch sizes, validation-loss comparisons, optimizer, and budget confirmation. R20 records only the divergent small-batch condition.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 4 BLEU values match the supplied text. Best scores occur at different epochs within a common 50-epoch budget. No uncertainty estimates are reported. E3 concerns shrinking SGD, so it does not substantiate the record's proposed limitation for shrunk Adam. The study is not an original source for either tested version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and their local connectivity.
Image-classification and word-level language-model benchmarks; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD.
Language models; large-batch behavior without CLR; longer training and the other recipe adaptations listed in the version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: INV schedule at Adam learning rate 3e-4 on IWSLT2014-de-en
relationships.reason: R5 gives Adam 30.46 BLEU versus SGD's 30.78 in R4.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower BLEU score for Adam than SGD remains unverified.

relationships.condition: INV schedule at the largest listed Adam learning rates on IWSLT2017-de-en and IWSLT2014-fr-en
relationships.reason: Adam reaches 28.94 versus SGD's 30.82 (R13, R9), and 6.20 versus 35.51 (R19, R18).
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower BLEU scores for Adam than SGD at the largest listed Adam learning rates remain unverified.

relationships.condition: INV schedule at moderate Adam learning rates on IWSLT2017-de-en
relationships.reason: R10 and R11 trail SGD in R9 by only 0.04 and 0.12 BLEU, with no uncertainty estimates.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam deficits of 0.04 and 0.12 BLEU remain unverified and lack uncertainty estimates.

relationships.reason: Adam CLR exceeds SGD CLR on both corpora: 32.65 versus 30.16 and 33.00 versus 30.40; shrunk Adam also exceeds those SGD scores.
relationships.display_finding: Reported advantages for Adam with CLR and shrunk Adam over SGD with CLR on both corpora remain unverified.

relationships.condition: INV on IWSLT2014-de-en at Adam 5e-4, and moderate-rate Adam configurations on IWSLT2014-fr-en
relationships.reason: R3 slightly exceeds R4; R14–R17 exceed SGD in R18, showing dependence on corpus, learning rate, and schedule.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam advantages over SGD in these corpus and learning-rate settings remain unverified.

relationships.condition: IWSLT2014-de-en with the adapted CLR recipe
relationships.reason: R20 and Section 4.3 report divergence at batch 256 and better validation performance with larger batches, consistent with V5's recipe-adaptation qualification.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports that training diverged at batch 256 and that larger batches gave better validation performance, but this comparison remains unverified.
